All three cases work. Screenshots under `prototypes/` (live: **http://maker:4001/duplicate.html**).

**Saving a link you already have** (`shot-32-dupe-exact.png`)
I tried to save the NYT link that's already in the list. Instead of creating a second copy, the app shows *"You already saved this as 'The Quiet Art of Reading Later' (saved 12 Jan 2026, To read). Taking you to it — no duplicate created,"* scrolls to that existing bookmark and **highlights it** — with its tags and note right there, so you remember why you kept it. The list count doesn't grow.

**Recognising the "same" link even when it looks different** (`shot-33-dupe-tracking.png`)
Here I saved the *same* article but typed as `nytimes.com/...?utm_source=twitter&utm_campaign=x#top` — no `https://`, no `www.`, extra tracking bits on the end, and a `#top` fragment. It's still recognised as the one you already have. I decided "the same link" should **ignore** these differences: `http` vs `https`, a leading `www.`, a trailing slash, capitalisation in the site name, common tracking parameters (`utm_...`, `fbclid`, etc.), and the `#section` fragment. **Does that match your sense of "the same link,"** or would you want any of those treated as genuinely different?

**When the existing one is archived** (`shot-34-dupe-archived.png`)
If the link you're re-saving is sitting in your Archive, the app still doesn't duplicate it — it tells you it's already there *in your Archive* and offers a one-click **Restore it**, so you're not left confused about why it "isn't in your list." Is surfacing + offering to restore the right move here, or would you rather it just quietly point you to the archived copy?

Two questions for you in there — the **normalization rules** (what counts as the same link) and the **archived-duplicate** behaviour. How do those sit with you?
